summary: A faithful Balancer V3 declarative Swap JSON is not expressible on 104ff465. The decisive gap is discovery: the Family declares a custom receipt/txHash nomination (filtered to the nominated pool) and an address-surface reverse binding (discovery.ts:61-62), while declarative mapped discovery has exactly one nomination discriminator (declarative-discovery.ts:69), only address-surface mode can declare reverse binding (declarative-discovery.ts:453-455), and tx-evidence mode has no per-nomination pool/block/token filter (tx-evidence-nomination.ts:44-60). A compile probe confirms tx-evidence + reverseBinding throws, address-surface + reverseBinding works but has no receipt nomination, and tx-evidence alone has reverseBinding explicitly-unsupported. Independent gaps remain in pricing (current first-success probe batch needs a result-dependent step condition; declarative-read-flow.ts:60-62) and identity (normalized-bytecode classification uses sha256 in local-model.ts/stable-surge.ts/vault-model.ts; declarative identity only exposes keccak codeHash/maskHash at declarative-values.ts:184,241). No prior JSON/math draft exists on backup-local-82bfc8fc; the recorded migration contract also excludes the disabled Balancer V2/V3 from the 15-Family JSON cutover. The handwritten production entry remains authoritative.

decisiveBlocker.capability: discovery must preserve both the custom receipt/txHash nomination filtered to the nominated pool and the address-surface reverse binding with code/Vault-membership checks

existingSource.fact: The Family declares evidenceChannel 'nominate', txSeedNominations true, sources landed-log/observed-call/address-surface, and a Vault.swap call pattern (the pool is tuple component 1).
The Family declares both a custom receipt nominate (nominateBalancerV3) and an implementation reverseBinding (reverseBindBalancerV3).

The custom nomination re-reads the nominated receipt, decodes Vault Swap logs and keeps only logs whose decoded pool equals nomination.address; the reverse binding checks pool code, getVault()==VAULT and isPoolRegistered, then emits an address-surface observation.

frameworkLimitation.fact: DeclarativeMappedDiscovery has a single nomination discriminator: 'tx-evidence' | 'address-surface'. There is no combined or filtered form.
tx-evidence always uses createTxEvidenceNomination({allMatches:true, acceptObservation}); acceptObservation only decodes a candidate, it cannot filter by nomination address, block or token pair.
reverseBinding is rejected unless nomination === 'address-surface' and a surface is declared; reverse binding cannot be combined with tx-evidence.

allMatches emits every declared-topic receipt log/call whose decoded candidate is accepted; opaque nomination fields are never used to enforce the pool/block/token guards of the legacy custom nominate.

recentCallNomination is not equivalent: it scans recent logs for a 32-byte topic key and traces a call; it does not re-read the nominated txHash receipt and cannot apply the Family's per-nomination pool/block/token filter. It is also only available on the address-surface nomination mode.

probe.method: Temporary tsx probe (removed) compiled a v2 mapping with a top-level-address call pattern and tested each nomination mode/reverse-binding combination.

results.nomination tx-evidence + reverseBinding: THROW: 'reverse binding requires a declared address-surface nomination'
results.nomination address-surface + reverseBind: OK, reverseBinding=implementation, txSeedNominations=undefined (no txHash receipt nomination)
OK, reverseBinding=implementation, txSeedNominations=true, nominate remains the address-surface nominate (no receipt/txHash nomination)

probe.consequence: A JSON must choose one nomination path. tx-evidence drops the verified reverse binding; address-surface drops the receipt/txHash nomination. The generic allMatches path also loses the legacy per-nomination pool/block/token filter. recentCallNomination is a different recent-log/trace path, not a faithful substitute.

whyPartialCutoverIsNotAcceptable: The Family declares both paths as supported (discovery.ts:61-62); the recorded strict/Ready evidence and production universe reverse-binding path rely on them.
Choosing tx-evidence makes reverse binding explicitly unsupported and nominates every matching Vault market in a receipt, changing the evidence scope.
Choosing address-surface loses the nominated txHash receipt re-read; recentCallNomination's recent-log scan/trace is not the same evidence shape and cannot enforce the legacy opaque filters.
A cutover that silently drops either path narrows a supported discovery/settlement-adjacent capability, which the task forbids.

existingSource.fact: For non-local pools, round 0 issues only the first probe; after reading current-quote:0, round 1 decides whether to return null or issue the remaining probes. The batch shape depends on prior quote results.

frameworkLimitation.fact: A read-flow step 'when' may only reference invocation inputs, never $steps/prior results; only requests/results/decode can reference prior steps. A JSON flow cannot condition the second probe batch on the first quote.

additionalBlockers.consequence: All probes would have to be issued up front (with required:false and decode filtering), changing the RPC batch count/order and issuing amounts the original stops before; this is a behavior/cost deviation, not the same pricing path. The same limitation class was decisive for balancer-v2.

existingSource.fact: Local pool model classification masks compiler immutables and compares sha256(normalized runtime) against model-template normalizedCodeSha256.
StableSurge hook and pool classification use sha256(normalized runtime) plus immutable value checks.
Vault/extension/admin classification also compares sha256(normalized runtime) and validates constructor immutables/timing.

frameworkLimitation.fact: Declarative identity exposes keccak256 via codeHash and maskHash, not sha256 of normalized bytecode. A family math model could reproduce the legacy classifier, but that moves identity classification into an opaque family TS model rather than a declarative identity proof; it is not an equivalent JSON identity.

additionalBlockers.consequence: The local-model/StableSurge/Vault proof cannot be declared with existing identity value ops. Replacing sha256 with precomputed keccak hashes would change the Family's content-hash algorithm; retaining it requires family-specific code outside the declarative identity.

existingSource.fact: A decoded Vault Swap log invalidates only that pool's routes; undecodable Vault logs invalidate all state-only weighted routes; Vault calls invalidate those routes.

frameworkLimitation.fact: Declarative mutation indexes match addresses; affectedStateKeys maps matched entries to state keys. Per-instance mutationPredicate can accept/reject an observation, but there is no declared event-payload-to-pool projection at the index level.

additionalBlockers.consequence: A JSON mutation declaration can conservatively invalidate all routes on any Vault log (or use a family math predicate that decodes the log), changing selective refresh behavior and cost.

additionalBlockers.severity: behavior parity to review if discovery/identity are unblocked

existingSource.fact: refreshPolicyForInstance is on-touch only for proven state-only weighted pools; other pools refresh each block.

Local exact uses sequential trial state only when tokens are plain, no hook addresses are present and no rate providers/yield-fee transitions are involved; otherwise it still returns a local quote with an unsupported trial-state reason.

frameworkLimitation.fact: Declarative pricing exposes refreshPolicyForInstance per selected variant; the variant declaration is static, so a conditional on-touch/each-block policy needs separate variants or accepts the conservative each-block policy.

additionalBlockers.consequence: The local trial-state split can likely be expressed with a conditional trialState module plus localStateUnsupportedReason, but refresh policy and exact classification need a family-specific review; not the decisive blocker.

nonBlockingAnalysis.note: Structural observations only; none is a validated implementation or acceptance claim.
expressibleWithJsonPlusFamilyMath: Vault.swap observed call: a probe compiled a mapped call pattern using the Vault target as the candidate address field plus the pool from tuple component 1 via an ABI path; the candidate key/instance key must include vault+pool, which differs from the legacy pool-only candidate shape but is expressible.
Discovery Swap event: Vault Swap event log with pool/tokenIn/tokenOut indexed and amount/fee fields; canonical ABI, predicates, pool materialization and swap observation can be declared.

Identity stages: get-code for pool/vault/router/permit2/extension/admin, getPermit2, getVault, isPoolRegistered, getPoolTokenInfo, getHooksConfig, decimals, hook-code; evidence phases and retryable unsupported-hook decision can follow the existing identity.
Routes/instance: all ordered token pairs, pool graph venue, binding key/fingerprint, runtime source-state/quote-completion requirements.

Execution: v2 steps can reproduce token.approve(0/amount/0), Permit2.approve(amount/0), Router.swapSingleTokenExactIn and direct executor output; effects can check actual input debit/output credit and unchanged native.

Local pricing/exact: family math can wrap the existing FixedPoint/StableMath/WeightedMath, decode getPoolData, compute probe amounts, and provide quote/transition and pricingProjection rows; the math.ts + append-only registry mechanism already supports nested arrays/objects.
Router pricing/exact: querySwapSingleTokenExactIn is a single return uint256, so a view chain quote can prove the amount; sender is an ABI argument and can be executor/zero as in the legacy paths.
deviationsStillToReviewIfUnblocked: The Vault.swap candidate needs vault+pool in its key/instanceKey rather than the legacy pool-only candidate; identity would need to keep the pool field as its subject while accepting the vault field.

The generated action adapter would carry the declarative runtime program, not the handwritten multi-call action encoding; family-dual-execution asserts the exact approve/permit/swap call order, which must be reproduced by execution.steps before claiming parity.

The local math/fixed-point and bytecode template data would need to move into a family math module or be retained as legacy family TS; keeping sha256 classification in TS is a family-code dependency, not a JSON identity proof.
The Family is disabled by default and outside the recorded 15-Family Swap JSON cutover; activation and generated-catalog authorization are separate decisions.
